findings.source_passage: Some of them have little boxes of dentistical-looking implements, specially intended for the skrimshandering business. But, in general, they toil with their jack-knives alone
findings.why_it_matters: The 'dentistical-looking implements' detail is a characteristic Melvillean comic aside that establishes the narrator's voice; its loss flattens the passage into bare summary.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'Some of them have little boxes of dentistical-looking implements' before the jack-knife line to preserve the comic register.

findings.source_passage: they will turn you out anything you please, in the way of a mariner's fancy
findings.why_it_matters: This closing flourish is a voice-defining phrase that gives the scrimshander paragraph its warm, admiring conclusion; dropping it leaves the paragraph truncated without a landing.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'and with that almost omnipotent tool of the sailor, they will turn you out anything you please, in the way of a mariner's fancy' to the scrimshander paragraph.

findings.source_passage: For, with but a bit of broken sea-shell or a shark's tooth, that miraculous intricacy of wooden net-work has been achieved; and it has cost steady years of steady application.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is the argumentative and rhetorical pivot of the Hawaiian–sailor-savage comparison; omitting it removes the evidence that makes the Latin-lexicon analogy persuasive.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the sea-shell/steady-application sentence between the Latin-lexicon comparison and the transition to the white sailor-savage.

findings.source_passage: When the porter is sleepy, the anvil-headed whale would be best. But these knocking whales are seldom remarkable as faithful essays.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'porter is sleepy / anvil-headed whale' quip is a signature Melvillean comic digression; its erasure strips the catalogue of its characteristic wry humor.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'When the porter is sleepy, the anvil-headed whale would be best. But these knocking whales are seldom remarkable as faithful essays.' in the knockers sentence.

findings.source_passage: besides that are to all intents and purposes so labelled with "Hands off!" you cannot examine them closely enough to decide upon their merit.
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical 'Hands off!' label is a dry joke that defines the tone of the whole catalogue; compressing it to a bare list erases the ironic commentary on these unexaminable specimens.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 'Hands off! / cannot examine them closely enough' clause when mentioning the spire weather-cocks.

findings.source_passage: to see whether the fabled heavens with all their countless tents really lie encamped beyond my mortal sight!
findings.why_it_matters: The final clause 'to see whether the fabled heavens with all their countless tents really lie encamped beyond my mortal sight!' is the chapter's cosmic climax; without it the closing sentence ends mid-gesture.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full final sentence: 'would I could mount that whale and leap the topmost skies, to see whether the fabled heavens with all their countless tents really lie encamped beyond my mortal sight!'

summary: The draft preserves the chapter's skeleton and several key verbatim passages but consistently strips the comic asides and rhetorical elaborations that give the catalogue its Melvillean voice, with four medium-severity voice-flattening losses triggering the regenerate threshold.
